intro: Newark pickup leaves the Elizabeth warehouse on weekday mornings. Essex County is close enough that a rug is often on a truck the same week the quote is approved.
pickupNote: Most stops are street-level or a short lobby carry. Tell us if the building needs a loading dock appointment.
turnaround: Same-week pickup is common. A wool wash is still two to three weeks, because the rug has to dry before it comes back.

faq.question: Do Newark routes start in the city?
faq.answer: They start at the Elizabeth warehouse and run through Newark on weekday mornings.

intro: Jersey City waterfront towers along the Hudson usually need a freight elevator booked before the crew leaves Elizabeth. We will not guess the elevator from the street address.
pickupNote: Send the freight elevator hours with the quote. A residential elevator that stops at 4 p.m. changes the window.
turnaround: Once the elevator is reserved, pickup is a North Jersey weekday. Cleaning still waits on drying time at the warehouse.

faq.question: Can you meet a freight elevator in Jersey City?
faq.answer: Yes, if the reservation is in the quote. We do not arrive and hope the elevator is free.

intro: Hoboken brownstones are the usual carry: a parlor-floor turn and a stair that is steeper than it looks from the sidewalk. The quote asks about that turn before we price the pickup.
pickupNote: Street parking turns over quickly. A morning window is easier than a late afternoon stop.
turnaround: Pickup is on the North Jersey route. Plan on the same wash time as Newark once the rug is in Elizabeth.

faq.question: Do Hoboken stairs change the quote?
faq.answer: Yes. A walk-up is a different job from a curb handoff, and the quote names which one you are booking.

intro: Manhattan deliveries are scheduled from Elizabeth with a two-hour window. Elevator buildings can ask for a certificate of insurance, and we send it when the quote is approved.
pickupNote: Tell us the cross street and whether the service entrance is on a different block from the lobby.
turnaround: The truck is a scheduled Manhattan run, not a same-day van. A cleaned rug returns on a later window after it is dry.

faq.question: Do you carry a certificate of insurance for Manhattan buildings?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for it in the quote and we send it before the delivery day.

intro: Brooklyn brownstones and walk-ups mean a stoop carry. We price the stairs in the quote, not after the truck is at the curb.
pickupNote: Name the stoop, the parlor floor, and any gate. A garden entrance is a different path from the front door.
turnaround: Brooklyn rides the same Elizabeth route as Manhattan, on its own stops. Wash time is still set by drying, not by the bridge.

faq.question: Is a Brooklyn stoop included in pickup?
faq.answer: The quote includes the carry you describe. A last-minute walk-up that was not in the notes is a new quote.

intro: Philadelphia is a longer run from Elizabeth than North Jersey. Center City loading docks need a morning slot, and we book that slot before the rug leaves the warehouse.
pickupNote: Rittenhouse walk-ups and dock buildings are different jobs. Say which one the address is.
turnaround: Add a transit day beyond a Newark stop. The wash itself is still done in Elizabeth and does not start until the rug arrives.

faq.question: Why is Philadelphia slower than Newark?
faq.answer: The rug travels from Elizabeth. The extra day is the road, not a different cleaning process.

intro: Pittsburgh is farther from Elizabeth than Philadelphia, so we batch western Pennsylvania. A single rug does not ride as its own overnight.
pickupNote: Hill streets and tight row-house stairs belong in the notes. We ask before we put the stop on a batch.
turnaround: Expect a longer wait for the truck than in Philadelphia. Once the rug is in Elizabeth, drying sets the return date.

faq.question: Do you run to Pittsburgh every day?
faq.answer: No. Western Pennsylvania is a batched route from the New Jersey warehouse.

intro: Boston is a scheduled run from the New Jersey warehouse, not a same-day van. Beacon Hill stairs and streets that need a permit belong in the quote.
pickupNote: Tell us if the building requires a permit or a specific loading street. We do not discover that at the curb.
turnaround: The Boston truck is weekly, not daily. A wash still takes two to three weeks after the rug reaches Elizabeth.

faq.question: Is Boston served from a local shop?
faq.answer: No. Pickup and the work both run through the Elizabeth warehouse.

intro: Cambridge rides the Boston run, with narrower streets around the university squares. We ask which entrance faces the street before we quote the carry.
pickupNote: A side door on a one-way street needs a note. The driver does not circle the block looking for it.
turnaround: Same weekly truck as Boston. Cambridge is not a separate, faster route.

faq.question: Can you stop in Cambridge without a Boston address?
faq.answer: Yes. Cambridge is its own stop on the Boston run from Elizabeth.

intro: Atlanta stops leave the Fairburn warehouse. Inside the perimeter, placement is often two business days after the quote is approved, when the route has room.
pickupNote: Midtown towers need a loading dock time. Intown houses are usually a short carry from the drive.
turnaround: Fairburn is close, so the truck is the fast part. A wool wash still waits until the rug is dry.

faq.question: Where do Atlanta rugs get washed?
faq.answer: At the Fairburn warehouse, not in a storefront in the city.

intro: Savannah’s coastal air is hard on a damp wool rug. Washed pieces stay in Fairburn until they are dry, then ride the coastal route.
pickupNote: Historic-district squares can mean a longer carry from the nearest place a truck can stop. Say how far the door is from the curb.
turnaround: Add the coastal transit day to the drying time. We do not send a rug south while it is still damp.

faq.question: Will a cleaned rug leave Fairburn damp for Savannah?
faq.answer: No. It stays at the warehouse until it is dry, then it joins the coastal route.

intro: Charlotte is served from the Georgia warehouse, with an extra transit day compared with Atlanta. Uptown loading is a morning window.
pickupNote: South End walk-ups and uptown docks are different quotes. Name the floor and the elevator.
turnaround: The extra day is the drive from Fairburn. The wash clock starts when the rug arrives, not when we pick it up.

faq.question: Is Charlotte on the Atlanta truck?
faq.answer: It is a separate day from the inside-the-perimeter Atlanta stops.

intro: The Triangle is its own day from Fairburn, not a stop tacked onto Charlotte. We do not promise the Atlanta turnaround on a Raleigh ticket.
pickupNote: Downtown decks and suburban drives need different notes. A low deck clearance should be in the quote.
turnaround: Plan on the Georgia warehouse plus the Triangle transit day, then drying time before the return.

faq.question: Can a Raleigh rug share a Charlotte pickup day?
faq.answer: Not as a rule. Raleigh is scheduled as its own run from Fairburn.

intro: Miami is the longest Southeast run from Fairburn. Salt air and humidity mean a cleaned rug does not leave the warehouse damp.
pickupNote: Condo freight elevators and a lobby handoff are different jobs. Reserve the elevator before the truck is assigned.
turnaround: Transit is longer than Atlanta, and the rug waits in Fairburn until it is dry. The quote names both.

faq.question: Do you wash rugs in Miami?
faq.answer: No. The wash is in Fairburn. Miami is pickup and the return route.

intro: Tampa is a Gulf route from Fairburn, not the Miami truck. We ask about gated entries and elevator codes before the day is set.
pickupNote: A gate code that changes on the delivery morning delays the stop. Put the current code in the quote and update us if it changes.
turnaround: Gulf transit is its own day. Drying still happens in Georgia before the rug heads west across the state.

faq.question: Does Tampa share the Miami schedule?
faq.answer: No. The Gulf route is scheduled apart from the Miami run.

intro: Charleston historic-district houses often have a narrow stair and no freight elevator. The quote names that carry before we leave Fairburn.
pickupNote: A single house on a peninsula street may need the truck to stop a short walk away. Tell us where it can actually stand.
turnaround: The coastal day plus drying time. We do not shorten the wash to make a Charleston window.

faq.question: Can you carry a rug up a Charleston stair with a tight turn?
faq.answer: Only if the turn is described in the quote. If the rug will not make the turn, we say so before pickup.

intro: Columbia is inland from Charleston, on a different weekday from the same Georgia warehouse. The area around the state house is usually a short carry from the curb.
pickupNote: Campus and downtown stops are easier in the morning. Say if a deck or a service alley is the real entrance.
turnaround: Shorter on the road than Charleston, same drying rule in Fairburn.

faq.question: Is Columbia faster than Charleston?
faq.answer: The drive is shorter. The wash still finishes only when the rug is dry.

intro: Dallas and the surrounding stops run from Grand Prairie, close enough for a same-week route. High-rise freight elevators should be reserved before we roll.
pickupNote: A downtown dock and a Park Cities drive are different notes. Include the dock number or the gate.
turnaround: The truck can be the same week. A wash still takes the drying time at the Texas warehouse.

faq.question: Which warehouse washes a Dallas rug?
faq.answer: The Grand Prairie warehouse. It does not go to New Jersey for a wash.

intro: Austin deliveries leave Grand Prairie overnight. We ask about steep drives and tight stair turns before we quote, because those streets are the job.
pickupNote: A hill with a switchback driveway needs a photo or a clear note. We do not discover the grade at the curb.
turnaround: Add the overnight transit to the warehouse time. The return is another overnight after the rug is dry.

faq.question: Is Austin a same-day trip from Dallas?
faq.answer: No. It is an overnight run from Grand Prairie, out and back.

intro: Houston routes cover the Loop and nearby suburbs. Humidity is hard on a damp rug, so washed pieces stay in Grand Prairie until they are fully dry.
pickupNote: High-rises inside the Loop need a freight elevator. Suburban houses are usually a garage or a front door.
turnaround: Transit is longer than Dallas. The rug does not leave the warehouse damp just to make a Houston window.

faq.question: Will humidity in Houston change a fresh wash?
faq.answer: We keep the rug in Grand Prairie until it is dry, then we schedule the Houston return.

intro: Oklahoma City is a plains route from the Texas warehouse. We group Oklahoma stops so one rug is not the only piece on the truck.
pickupNote: Downtown garages and open suburban drives need the height clearance in the notes if the entrance is covered.
turnaround: The route is batched, so pickup waits for the Oklahoma day. Wash time starts in Grand Prairie after that.

faq.question: Do you keep a workshop in Oklahoma City?
faq.answer: No. The work is at the Texas warehouse. Oklahoma City is a pickup and return route.

intro: Tulsa uses the same Texas warehouse as Oklahoma City, on a different day. Downtown garages need a height clearance in the notes.
pickupNote: A covered entrance under 12 feet should be called out. The truck will not try a garage it cannot clear.
turnaround: Tulsa is not the Oklahoma City truck. Expect the batched day, then drying in Grand Prairie.

faq.question: Can a Tulsa rug ride with Oklahoma City?
faq.answer: They are different days from Grand Prairie, even though the warehouse is the same.

intro: Los Angeles routes start in Ontario. Hillside streets and long carries up steps are quoted separately from a curb drop.
pickupNote: A canyon road or a long exterior stair needs to be in the quote. The curb price does not include it.
turnaround: The Ontario warehouse sets the wash time. The city truck is the delivery, not the place the rug is washed.

faq.question: Are hillside steps part of a Los Angeles pickup?
faq.answer: Only when they are in the quote. A curb drop and a stair carry are different prices, both by quote.

intro: San Diego is a scheduled run from the California warehouse, typically once or twice a week, not a daily van from Ontario.
pickupNote: Coastal condos often have a garage elevator. Reserve it, and tell us the floor, before the run is locked.
turnaround: Wait for the San Diego day, then the usual drying time in Ontario before the rug comes back.

faq.question: How often is the San Diego route?
faq.answer: Usually once or twice a week, depending on how full the Ontario schedule is.

intro: San Francisco hills and tight turns are the carry. A garage with a steep apron is a different quote from a lobby handoff.
pickupNote: Name the apron, the curb cut, and any stair from the garage to the door. We price the path you describe.
turnaround: The northern California run is less frequent than Los Angeles. Drying still happens in Ontario.

faq.question: Do you wash rugs in San Francisco?
faq.answer: No. Pickup is local to the route. The wash and the repair happen at the Ontario warehouse.

intro: Phoenix heat changes the day. We do not leave a wool rug in a closed truck through the afternoon, so the window is earlier than on the coast.
pickupNote: Tile roofs and long drives are not the issue. The issue is a rug sitting in a hot truck. Morning stops are the rule.
turnaround: The western route from Ontario, with a morning window. A wash still finishes only when the rug is dry.

faq.question: Why are Phoenix windows earlier?
faq.answer: A wool rug should not sit in a closed truck in the afternoon heat. We schedule the stop earlier.

intro: Tucson is farther than Phoenix on the same western route. Plan on a later arrival than a Phoenix stop booked on the same ticket.
pickupNote: Desert lots and gated communities need the gate instructions in the quote. The driver does not wait out a call box.
turnaround: Longer on the road than Phoenix, same Ontario warehouse for the wash, same rule about a hot truck.

faq.question: Does Tucson share Phoenix’s morning window?
faq.answer: The truck still avoids the hottest hours. Tucson is later on the route than Phoenix, so the window is the one we name in the quote.
